summary: Formal specification of the 5 discrete uncollapsed document evidence levels required to cross the Byte-Authority Barrier.

uncollapsedEvidenceLevels.definition: An official URL has been discovered on a government or public testing authority portal.
requiredProof: officialSourceUrl string matching http/https gov portal scheme

uncollapsedEvidenceLevels.definition: The specific official document identity (notice number, file name, portal listing row) is resolved.
The document binary payload has been downloaded and persisted into local/object storage.
The acquired bytes have been cryptographically hashed and verified with a valid 64-character hex SHA-256 digest.
disallowedClaims: TEXT_EXTRACTED_AND_BOUND (if scan text unresolved or unparsed)
uncollapsedEvidenceLevels.personalizationPermission: BLOCKED if text unresolved; permits generic public facts

uncollapsedEvidenceLevels.definition: Document text is machine-readable and extracted with verified page and paragraph offset bindings.
uncollapsedEvidenceLevels.personalizationPermission: ELIGIBLE to cross Byte-Authority Barrier for rule verification

governanceLaws: LAW 1 (NO COLLAPSE): URL_FOUND can never be collapsed into SHA256_VERIFIED or BYTES_ACQUIRED.
LAW 2 (BYTE-AUTHORITY BARRIER): Final ELIGIBLE / NOT_ELIGIBLE emitted only when source evidence is at least SHA256_VERIFIED with extracted text bound.
LAW 3 (ZERO DEFAULTING): Missing document proof defaults to lower tier; never promotes upwards.
LAW 4 (SCAN SAFETY): Scanned PDF with verified SHA256 remains at SHA256_VERIFIED / BYTE_VERIFIED; scanTextUnresolved blocks TEXT_EXTRACTED_AND_BOUND.
